company_items.summary: AutoZone reported FQ4 EPS of $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by a 145 basis point tariff refund tailwind and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit to gross margins. Domestic comps missed at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted positive sales linearity in the final 8 weeks and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional ~$106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80-90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal expands Cognex's footprint in the fast-growing robotics and AI-driven vision space.

MillerKnoll posted solid FQ1 EPS of 53 cents vs. the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even excluding the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, with adjusted EPS of 42 cents. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. the Street's $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed to $3.88-4.03 billion from $3.93-4.13 billion, while EPS guidance was held unchanged at $1.85-2.15.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau previously served as CFO at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International, bringing substantial large-cap industrial finance experience.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents vs. the Street's 87 cents, as gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% vs. the Street's 13.85%, and management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressures weighing on retail. Revenue came in at $2.311 billion, slightly above the Street's $2.17 billion estimate, and dealer inventory is described as healthy heading into fiscal 2027. Bright spots included a ~75% year-over-year surge in North American towable RV order backlog, though no formal fiscal 2027 guidance was provided.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, including an impressive 22% weight loss outcome. The strong data reinforces Viking's position as a credible competitor in the rapidly expanding obesity drug market.

tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday September 22nd, covering six names reporting before the open. Let's run through them.

Starting with AutoZone. The company posted a headline earnings beat — $56.05 per share versus the Street at $54.03 — but the quality of that beat is questionable. The upside was driven by tariff refunds, which added 145 basis points to gross margins, and a non-cash LIFO benefit worth another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the picture is less impressive. Domestic comps came in at plus 1.6%, well short of the Street's plus 3.1% expectation, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did note improving sales linearity in the back half of the quarter and said they feel well positioned for fiscal 2027 growth. Call this one mixed at best.

Cognex is making a move into Physical AI and robotics. The company announced the acquisition of RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception — for roughly 500 million dollars upfront plus another 106 million. RealSense is expected to generate 80 to 90 million in revenue, growing more than 50 percent year-over-year. This is a strategic expansion into high-growth territory and the market should view it constructively.

MillerKnoll delivered a solid quarter. EPS came in at 53 cents versus the Street at 36 cents, and importantly, even excluding an 11-cent tariff refund benefit, they still would have beaten at 42 cents. Sales missed, down 3.3% organically to $923 million versus expectations near $943 million, though orders grew 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year sales guidance was trimmed modestly, but EPS guidance held steady. Net-net, a mixed but generally decent print.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1st. Hau previously held the CFO role at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. This is a management transition, not a financial event — relatively neutral for now.

THOR Industries disappointed. FQ4 EPS came in at 78 cents versus 87 cents expected, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%, well below the Street's 13.85% estimate. Management was candid about the difficult environment — stubborn interest rates, high fuel costs, and inflation squeezing consumer budgets. No formal fiscal 2027 guidance was provided. The silver lining is that North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year and dealer inventories look healthy. But the headline miss and cautious tone make this one a headwind for the stock.

Finally, Viking Therapeutics is the standout mover this morning. Shares are spiking in pre-market after the company reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 weight loss drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss. That's a strong number and confirms Viking as a serious player in the obesity drug race. Expect significant upside follow-through at the open.

No broad macro commentary was included in today's note. The session's directional tone will largely be driven by these individual catalysts, with Viking the headline mover and AutoZone's quality-of-beat debate likely a key discussion point.
